name: Cholla Buds
caution: De-spine the buds thoroughly (roll and singe) before cooking; never eat them raw or spined. Never eat a wild plant on this guide's word alone. Confirm identity against several sources and learn the look-alikes first.

sections.title: Identification
sections.body: The cane cholla's spiny joints carry fat flower buds in spring. It is the buds, not the fruit, that are the traditional food.

sections.title: Uses
sections.body: Roll the buds to knock off spines, then boil or roast. A Southwestern staple, tangy and rich in calcium.
